ai.description: *Micrixalus adonis* is a small frog (21–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored venter. It is distinguished by a bright white throat and the male’s habit of foot-flagging near forest streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus adonis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, bright white-tipped third finger, which is conspicuously longer than in other similar *Micrixalus* species.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus adonis* inhabits the shaded, rocky streams of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Beautiful Dancing Frog is diurnal, with males performing rhythmic "foot-flagging" displays to attract mates and defend territories near fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus adonis* is an egg-laying frog that breeds during the monsoon season, depositing small clutches of eggs in hidden crevices within forest stream beds.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus adonis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting streams within the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Beautiful Dancing Frog produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing, rocky streams in tropical forests.
